title: Gingerbread Latte Cupcakes
shortDescription: Espresso gingerbread cupcakes with warm spice and a cream swirl frosting, ready in about 45 minutes from prep to bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a gingerbread latte in cake form. I mix strong espresso right into the batter so the coffee flavor is not shy. Molasses, ginger, cinnamon and cloves give the crumb that classic gingerbread warmth. A light cream swirl frosting on top balances the spice like the foam on a real latte. I tested this batch on a cold December afternoon with the oven running and coffee brewing at the same time. The kitchen smelled like a holiday cafe by the time they cooled. This is a great make ahead treat for a cookie swap or a coffee themed party. The flavor gets even better the next day.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon and cloves in a bowl.
Beat softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add molasses and eggs to the butter mix. Beat until smooth.
Mix in cooled espresso and buttermilk on low speed until combined.
Fold in the flour mix in two batches. Stop as soon as no streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For the frosting, beat cold heavy cream, mascarpone, powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Pipe the cream swirl frosting high on fully cooled cupcakes. Dust with cinnamon before serving.
tips: Use espresso, not weak drip coffee. The stronger brew keeps the coffee flavor from getting lost in the spice.
Chill your bowl and beaters before whipping the frosting so it holds a tall swirl.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting or the cream will melt and slide off.
Store frosted cupcakes in the fridge and let them sit 15 minutes at room temperature before eating.

faq.question: Can I use instant espresso powder instead of brewed espresso?
faq.answer: Yes. Dissolve 2 teaspoons of instant espresso powder in 1/2 cup hot water and cool it before adding to the batter.

faq.question: Will the coffee flavor be too strong for kids?
faq.answer: The espresso amount is small next to the batter, so the flavor reads more like gingerbread with a coffee hint than a strong coffee cake.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting ahead of time?
faq.answer: Make it up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Rewhip it for 30 seconds before piping to bring back the stiff peaks.

faq.question: What can I use instead of mascarpone in the frosting?
faq.answer: Full fat cream cheese works well as a swap. Bring it to room temperature first so the frosting stays smooth.

conclusion: These gingerbread latte cupcakes bring coffee shop warmth into your own kitchen. Serve them at your next holiday gathering with a real latte on the side.
